# Accessible by default

> How much of accessibility the modern web platform handles natively — with
> little to no JavaScript. An interactive argument in four chapters: the
> standard (WCAG on the timeline it grew on, each criterion with a working
> break-this-rule demo), the craft (accessible-default decisions in modern
> CSS and native HTML), a CSS showcase grouped by Baseline support, and the
> proof (testing as a layered job). By Thomas Sweet.

The pages are rendered HTML. The markdown under /llms/ is generated from the
same registries that render the pages, so it cannot drift from the live demos.

## Docs

- [SKILL.md](https://accessible-by-default.dev/llms/SKILL.md): the decisions,
  written for coding agents — what to reach for, what never to break, how to
  guard a feature that is not Baseline yet, and the ways this usually goes wrong
- [wcag-criteria.md](https://accessible-by-default.dev/llms/wcag-criteria.md):
  the success criteria most often broken by hand-built components, each with
  its requirement and who pays when it is missed
- [modern-css.md](https://accessible-by-default.dev/llms/modern-css.md): every
  showcased feature grouped by Baseline tier, with its @supports condition and
  the accessibility problem it solves
- [css-snippets.md](https://accessible-by-default.dev/llms/css-snippets.md):
  the accessible implementation of each feature, dependency-free and
  copy-paste ready

## Pages

- [The standard](https://accessible-by-default.dev/standard.html): WCAG on an
  explorable timeline, with break-this-rule demos per criterion
- [The craft](https://accessible-by-default.dev/craft.html): the
  accessible-default decisions in modern CSS and native HTML
- [CSS showcase](https://accessible-by-default.dev/showcase.html): modern CSS
  grouped by Baseline support, written as progressive enhancement
- [The proof](https://accessible-by-default.dev/proof.html): layered testing —
  automation's limits, the accessibility tree, filing what you find
- [Glossary](https://accessible-by-default.dev/glossary.html): short, honest
  definitions of the vocabulary the site leans on
- [Screen reader basics](https://accessible-by-default.dev/screen-reader.html):
  the keystrokes that matter and a fifteen-minute plan for hearing a page
- [DevTools for accessibility](https://accessible-by-default.dev/devtools.html):
  the audit tooling built into the browser, and the three add-ons that add
  something the panels can't

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ThomasSweet/a11y-foundation): source
  for everything above, including the installable agent skill
- [Style guide](https://accessible-by-default.dev/styleguide.html): the design
  tokens and components the site is drawn with
